name: The laws of memory, human and machine
heading: laws? of memory

laws.name: Recency and primacy
laws.ask: is the important thing first or last, never buried in the middle, and is the recent thing findable?
laws.source: Kahana, Diamond & Aka, Laws of Human Memory (PsyArXiv, draft 2022-07-01); Ebbinghaus 1885, the forgetting curve.

laws.name: Contiguity and similarity
laws.ask: is it stored next to what it will be recalled with, and is a look-alike that must stay separate kept separate?
laws.source: Kahana, Diamond & Aka, Laws of Human Memory (PsyArXiv, draft 2022-07-01).

laws.name: Repetition and spacing
laws.ask: is a thing that must stick re-surfaced on a schedule, not re-read once?
laws.source: Kahana, Diamond & Aka, Laws of Human Memory (PsyArXiv, draft 2022-07-01); Ebbinghaus 1885, the spacing effect.

laws.name: Cue-driven, encoding–retrieval
laws.ask: is it stored under the cue it will be asked for under?
laws.source: Surprenant & Neath, Principles of Memory (Psychology Press, 2009).

laws.name: Cue overload and relative distinctiveness
laws.ask: how many things share this cue, and does this one stand out among them?
laws.source: Surprenant & Neath, Principles of Memory (Psychology Press, 2009).

laws.name: Reconstruction and impurity
laws.ask: is a recalled thing marked as recalled, and does it carry its provenance?
laws.source: Surprenant & Neath, Principles of Memory (Psychology Press, 2009); Schacter, The seven sins of memory (American Psychologist, 1999; update Memory, 2022), misattribution and bias.

laws.name: Jost and Ribot
laws.ask: is the newest memory treated as the most fragile, and does consolidation get time before anything is trusted?
laws.source: Wixted, On Common Ground: Jost's (1897) law of forgetting and Ribot's (1881) law of retrograde amnesia (Psychological Review, 2004).

laws.name: Working memory is small
laws.ask: how many things does this ask a person, or a context window, to hold at once?
laws.source: Miller 1956, The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two (Psychological Review); Cowan's revision to about four chunks.

laws.name: Locality
laws.ask: is the hot set small and near, the cold set cheap and far?
laws.source: Denning, The Locality Principle (Communications of the ACM 48(7), 2005).

laws.name: The five-minute rule
laws.ask: what is re-used often enough to stay resident, and was that interval measured, not assumed?
laws.source: Gray & Putzolu 1985/87; Gray & Graefe 1997; Graefe 2007, the five-minute rule.

laws.name: Little's law
laws.ask: how much is in flight, and for how long?
laws.source: Little 1961, L = λW.

laws.name: Bélády
laws.ask: can adding memory make this worse under the policy chosen?
laws.source: Bélády 1969, the anomaly: more frames can mean more faults under a bad replacement policy.

laws.name: The memory wall
laws.ask: what waits on memory, and how often?
laws.source: Wulf & McKee 1995, the memory wall (ACM SIGARCH Computer Architecture News; excerpt via the Springer Encyclopedia of Parallel Computing).

laws.name: The log first
laws.ask: is the write appended and read back before it is trusted, and is every other copy a follower?
laws.source: write-ahead logging; Kreps 2013, "The Log" (LinkedIn Engineering); this house's append-never-overwrite, read-back law.

laws.name: Cache invalidation
laws.ask: which copy is canon, and does every other copy know when it went stale?
laws.source: Karlton, via Fowler, one of the two hard things in computer science; this house's move-the-source-of-truth, let-followers-follow law.

laws.name: Tiering
laws.ask: which tier and which function does this live in, and what promotes it?
laws.source: CoALA (Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan & Griffiths, 2023); "Memory in the Age of AI Agents" survey, the three axes.

laws.name: Remember the decision
laws.ask: does what is kept preserve the distinctions that change a decision?
laws.source: "Remember the Decision, Not the Description" (arXiv 2605.10870).

laws.name: Governed consolidation
laws.ask: is consistency verified before consolidation, does age decay it, and is what enters long-term memory controlled and attributed?
laws.source: SSGM, Governing Evolving Memory in LLM Agents (arXiv 2603.11768); Mem0, State of AI Agent Memory 2026.

laws.name: A window is not a history
aliases: a window is not a history
laws.ask: does the reader know how far back it can see?
laws.source: this house, earned

laws.name: The index is not the content
aliases: the index is not the content
laws.ask: does the index carry pointers only?
laws.source: this house, earned

laws.name: Promotion is his
laws.ask: whose words are these, and who may promote them?
laws.source: this house, earned

laws.name: Supersede, never erase
laws.ask: is a retired fact retired by a pointer, or by an erasure?
laws.source: this house, earned
